# A test picks a radio's option by the value it holds, through the target's
# override of the radio's @change, which calls what pressing the option's
# button calls. The options hold an int labeled otherwise, so a value is never
# taken for a label. fyne and bubbletea render no radio yet, so there is no
# option of one to pick.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component fitting ui.node {
    var fit = 1
    var heard list[int] = []

    ui.radio #fits(:value=fit, @change(v) { heard.push(v) }) {
        ui.choice(label="Snug", value=1)
        ui.choice(label="Loose", value=2)
    }
    ui.text(value="{fit}")
}

func testARadioChangePicksTheOptionHolding(t test.Test, c fitting) {
    c.fits.change(2)
    t.assert(c.fit == 2)
    t.assert(c.heard.length() == 1 && c.heard[0] == 2)
}

ui.window {
    fitting
}
